English: Reed Hive
Primitive bee skeps woven from reeds, set on the fringes of the camp. The beginning of beekeeping in the wild Slavic lands.
Clay Hive
Improved hives shaped from local clay, providing better insulation and protection for bee colonies. A modest step toward reliable honey yields.
Wicker Apiary
A cluster of portable wicker hives, enabling the movement of colonies with the clan. Honey output grows as beekeeping knowledge spreads.
Timber Hive House
A sturdy wooden structure housing advanced hives and tools, protecting bees and honey stores from weather and raiders. Marked progress in Slavic apiculture.
Honey Stand
A busy market stall for selling honey and beeswax, drawing traders and boosting clan prosperity. A sign of growing trade and prestige.
Wax Pavilion
A grand tent for processing and storing wax and honey, centralizing production and attracting distant merchants. A hub of economic activity.
Bee Breeders Room
A specialized chamber for nurturing queen bees and selecting the strongest colonies, increasing yields and bee health across the clan.
Market Apiary
A fortified market outpost for honey and beeswax trade, with dedicated guards and scribes. Establishes the clan as a regional honey power.
Master Beekeepers Hall
A grand meeting hall for the most skilled apiarists. Here, knowledge is shared and beekeeping techniques perfected, ensuring unmatched honey riches.
West Slavic Apiary Guild
The revered guild of Slavic apiarists. Its organization ensures clan unity, honey mastery, and a lasting legacy amid the wilds.
